definition: The middle phase of a Pulse transit run — operating speed, full vacuum, no acceleration or deceleration. The passenger experience is of perfect stillness: no vibration from external air (there is no air), no mechanical noise, no sense of motion. Just a sealed cylinder with a low 8 Hz coil tick and 40 minutes of whatever you choose to do with them. Experienced Pulse riders consider coasting the only genuinely pleasant part of transit. It is also the part that unnerves first-timers most — the absence of sensation at Mach 6 registers psychologically as something having gone wrong.
origin: Pulse transit culture, derived from nautical usage (coasting = moving with minimal effort along a shore)
usage: Pulse traveler jargon; also used metaphorically for any period of effortless forward motion in life or work.
example: "Once you're coasting, forget where you're going. The tube doesn't care and neither should you."
